newsitem.title: ITALY: Mother Teresa well, resting after health scare.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa well, resting after health scare.

text.p: Mother Teresa of Calcutta was in good condition and resting on Friday after a health scare when she needed oxygen on arrival at Rome airport, her order said.
"She is well. She is resting," said Sister Elena, head of the Italian branch of Mother Teresa's order of nuns.
She told Reuters that Mother Teresa's Italian doctor, Vincenzo Bilotta, had left the convent where the nun is staying in a poor area of Rome.
The 86-year-old nun, known as the saint of the gutters for her work with the destitute, was given oxygen for about 20 minutes in a VIP lounge at Rome airport after arriving from New Delhi.
"She had some oxygen because she was tired," said Giancarlo Fanti, a member of the medical team who assisted the Nobel peace prize winner at the airport.
"It was a long trip but there is no cause for worry. She was very happy, in good spirits and wanted to talk. Everything is in order," he said.
Bilotta also said there was no reason for alarm.
"I found her in good condition. The oxygen is a normal procedure for someone like her," Bilotta said. An ambulance was waiting outside in case of emergencies.

Mother Teresa, making her first foreign trip since she suffered serious health problems last year, blessed and smiled at reporters as she was taken in a wheelchair to a waiting car, which she was able to enter unaided.
The highlights of her visit to Rome are a meeting with Pope John Paul, not yet scheduled, and an initiation ceremony where new nuns will take their vows.

One of the purposes of her visit to the 76-year-old Pope is to introduce Sister Nirmala, who took over as superior-general of the Calcutta-based Missionaries of Charity in March when Mother Teresa stepped down after a battle against heart disease.
Mother Teresa was admitted to hospital three times last year for emergency care and heart surgery.
Her first public appearance is scheduled for the first of the two initiation ceremonies on May 23 but aides said she would most likely leave the convent before, health permitting.
Mother Teresa has said she would also like to accompany the Pope to Poland for part of his visit there next month and perhaps travel to the United States if she is well enough.
Italian families adopting four Indian children who arrived with the nun on the flight from New Delhi were at the airport.
"She blessed this new family of ours," said an Italian woman who adopted a 20-month-old girl named Romina Maria.
Doctor Patricia Aubanel, who was part of the team that operated on Mother Teresa in 1991, 1993 and 1996, told reporters in India this week that she had advised the nun to limit her trip to Rome.
Mother Teresa's recent tours outside India have been marred by ill health.

On a visit to Europe in 1993, she injured three ribs in a fall. On a trip to the United States in 1991, she fell ill midway through the visit and had to undergo the first of her three heart operations.
